title: How to Calculate the Mat Tinkler Salary: Hourly to Annual, Tax, and Super
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week, then apply tax and super. The mat tinkler salary example shows the method.
salarySummary: The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week yields an annual gross of $52,270.72 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $26.44 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,270.72 per year. This is gross pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect the annual calculation?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. If you select the casual loading option on the timesheet, the calculator adds 25% to the base rate before converting to annual. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is tax and Medicare levy applied to the annual figure?
faqs.a: The 2026–27 resident tax rates apply: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The take-home pay estimate deducts these from the annual gross, using the full tax-free threshold and single Medicare reduction thresholds from 2025–26.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you are checking your own wage or looking up a well-known figure like the mat tinkler salary, the basic formula is the same: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This gives you the gross annual pay before any deductions. For a standard full-time employee, the Fair Work Ombudsman and most awards assume a 38-hour week. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor for award-free employees. Most workers are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates for specific industries and roles. The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database with all classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

For casual employees, a 25% loading is added on top of the base rate. For example, the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour. When using the [timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate and then check the casual loading box – never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

### Annual Gross Calculation Example

Take the National Minimum Wage: $26.44 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,270.72 per year. If you are curious about a specific figure such as the mat tinkler salary, you can apply the same method using the known hourly rate. The on-site reference does not provide that exact salary, but the conversion formula works for any base rate.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For the National Minimum Wage, that is $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 before tax. The [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman site list weekly rates, so doubling them gives the fortnightly figure.

## Tax and the Medicare Levy

The annual gross figure is the starting point for tax calculations. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of the excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45% of the excess over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimate on this site uses the single reduction thresholds from 2025–26 because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of the reference data. For a single person earning $52,270.72, the tax would be approximately $5,110 (15% on $34,070) plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving a net annual figure of about $46,115.

## Superannuation Guarantee

Super is paid on top of your gross salary, not deducted from it. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For the National Minimum Wage example, the super contribution would be $52,270.72 × 12% = $6,272.49, paid by the employer into your super fund. This is separate from your take-home pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Award Rates vs. Market Rates

The figures above are legal minimums. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 per year. Many roles pay above the award rate. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context. When comparing a salary offer, always check the applicable award or enterprise agreement.

## Using the Calculator

The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether to add casual loading. It then calculates annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax and Medicare, and super. The result is an estimate – it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates or allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For a precise determination, consult the relevant award or a qualified advisor.

### Summary

To find the annual equivalent of any hourly rate, use the formula: hourly × hours per week × 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage gives $52,270.72 gross. Apply the 2026–27 tax scale and 2% Medicare to estimate take-home pay. Super is an additional 12% paid by the employer. Whether you are checking your own wage or researching the mat tinkler salary, this method provides a reliable starting point.
